**Ollama context window**: Ollama's `/v1` route ignores `num_ctx` and runs at 4096 tokens, silently cutting the start of long input. A provider with id or type `ollama` is therefore sent to the native `POST {base_url minus /v1}/api/chat` (NDJSON, same deltas; the final frame's `prompt_eval_count`/`eval_count` become usage) with `options.num_ctx` = the smallest bucket of [8192, 16384, 32768] (override: `providers.<id>.num_ctx_buckets`; filtered to `num_ctx_max` and `model_max_ctx`, falling back to the cap if none fit) that holds the prompt estimate (chars/3.5) plus a 1024 reply reserve. Ollama reloads the model (13-23 s) whenever `num_ctx` changes, so it is sticky: per process and per (provider, base_url, model) a request never sends a smaller `num_ctx` than the last one (it only grows; `aesop ask` is one-shot, so it gets bucketing only). When a request grows the bucket, `notify` emits `growing model window to N (Ollama reloads the model; this can take ~20 s)`. Concurrent asks of different buckets can still force a reload; keep agent prompts within one bucket or set `num_ctx_buckets` to a single value (e.g. `[16384]`). When the prompt alone exceeds the largest bucket, `notify` emits `warning: input ~N tokens exceeds the model window M; the start will be cut` before the reply (chat transcript; `aesop ask` wires `notify` to stderr, exit code unchanged). Other providers are untouched. Tests: `tests/chat-ollama-context.test.mjs`.
